name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MOLECULAR_BASIS_OF_INHERITANCE_MCQ_Q01 - Match organism with genomic base pair content

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Organism) List-II (Genetic Content)
A. \(\phi \times 174\) bacteriophage I. \(4.6 \times 10^{6}\text{ bp}\)
B. Bacteriophage lambda II. \(5386\text{ nucleotides}\)
C. Escherichia coli III. \(3.3 \times 10^{9}\text{ bp}\)
D. Human haploid genome IV. \(48502\text{ bp}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The task requires matching distinct organisms with their characteristic DNA lengths as defined by the number of nucleotides or base pairs.

Step 2: Relevant Principles and Values
The length of DNA is defined by the number of nucleotides or base pairs characteristic of each organism. Specifically:
- Bacteriophage \(\phi \times 174\) has a single-stranded circular DNA genome containing \(5386\text{ nucleotides}\).
- Bacteriophage lambda has a double-stranded linear genome of \(48502\text{ base pairs}\) (\(\text{bp}\)).
- The bacterium Escherichia coli contains \(4.6 \times 10^{6}\text{ bp}\).
- The haploid genome of Homo sapiens contains \(3.3 \times 10^{9}\text{ bp}\) (whereas the diploid content is \(6.6 \times 10^{9}\text{ bp}\)).

Step 3: Pairing Identification
- \(\phi \times 174\) bacteriophage associates with \(5386\text{ nucleotides}\).
- Bacteriophage lambda associates with \(48502\text{ bp}\).
- Escherichia coli associates with \(4.6 \times 10^{6}\text{ bp}\).
- Human haploid genome associates with \(3.3 \times 10^{9}\text{ bp}\).

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
All base pair and nucleotide quantities align precisely with the established molecular values for these model organisms.
Final Answer: The correct matching is \(\phi \times 174\) bacteriophage with \(5386\text{ nucleotides}\); Bacteriophage lambda with \(48502\text{ bp}\); Escherichia coli with \(4.6 \times 10^{6}\text{ bp}\); and Human haploid genome with \(3.3 \times 10^{9}\text{ bp}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MOLECULAR_BASIS_OF_INHERITANCE_MCQ_Q02 - Match scientist with historical molecular discovery

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Scientist) List-II (Contribution)
A. Friedrich Meischer I. X-ray diffraction data of DNA
B. James Watson and Francis Crick II. First identified DNA as an acidic substance called Nuclein
C. Erwin Chargaff III. Proposed the Double Helix model of DNA
D. Maurice Wilkins and Rosalind Franklin IV. Base ratio equality between Adenine-Thymine and Guanine-Cytosine

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The problem requires matching prominent historical researchers in molecular genetics with their direct contributions to the discovery and structural elucidation of DNA.

Step 2: Relevant Principles and Discoveries
- Friedrich Meischer (1869) was the first to identify DNA as an acidic substance located inside cell nuclei and termed it 'Nuclein'.
- James Watson and Francis Crick (1953) formulated and proposed the famous Double Helix structural model for DNA.
- Erwin Chargaff observed that in double-stranded DNA, the ratios between Adenine and Thymine, as well as Guanine and Cytosine, remain constant and equal to one (\(A/T = 1\) and \(G/C = 1\)).
- Maurice Wilkins and Rosalind Franklin generated crucial X-ray diffraction photographic data that provided structural measurements for Watson and Crick's model.

Step 3: Pairing Identification
- Friedrich Meischer associates with first identifying DNA as an acidic substance called Nuclein.
- James Watson and Francis Crick associate with proposing the Double Helix model of DNA.
- Erwin Chargaff associates with base ratio equality between Adenine-Thymine and Guanine-Cytosine.
- Maurice Wilkins and Rosalind Franklin associate with X-ray diffraction data of DNA.

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
Each historical milestone correctly matches the scientist who performed the work.
Final Answer: The correct matching is Friedrich Meischer with First identified DNA as an acidic substance called Nuclein; James Watson and Francis Crick with Proposed the Double Helix model of DNA; Erwin Chargaff with Base ratio equality between Adenine-Thymine and Guanine-Cytosine; and Maurice Wilkins and Rosalind Franklin with X-ray diffraction data of DNA.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MOLECULAR_BASIS_OF_INHERITANCE_MCQ_Q03 - Match classic genetic experiments with methodologies

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Experimenter) List-II (Experimental Setup / Discovery)
A. Frederick Griffith I. Semiconservative replication proof using \(^{15}\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}\) and CsCl gradient
B. Oswald Avery, Colin MacLeod, Maclyn McCarty II. Unequivocal proof of DNA as genetic material using \(^{32}\text{P}\) and \(^{35}\text{S}\)
C. Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase III. Transformation principle demonstrated in Streptococcus pneumoniae
D. Matthew Meselson and Franklin Stahl IV. Biochemical proof that DNase inhibits transformation whereas proteases do not

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Match landmark biological experiments with their exact experimental design and conclusions.

Step 2: Relevant Principles and Experiments
- Frederick Griffith (1928) injected mice with combinations of heat-killed virulent S strain and live non-virulent R strain of Streptococcus pneumoniae, discovering the phenomenon of transformation.
- Oswald Avery, Colin MacLeod, and Maclyn McCarty (1933-44) purified biochemicals from heat-killed S cells and established that only digestion with DNase inhibited transformation, proving that DNA was the transforming substance.
- Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase (1952) employed radioactive bacteriophages labeled with phosphorus-32 (labeling DNA) and sulfur-35 (labeling protein coat) to unequivocally prove that DNA enters the bacterium and serves as the genetic material.
- Matthew Meselson and Franklin Stahl (1958) grew E. coli in heavy nitrogen isotope (\(^{15}\text{N}\)) followed by \(^{14}\text{N}\), using CsCl density gradient centrifugation to demonstrate semiconservative replication of DNA.

Step 3: Pairing Identification
- Frederick Griffith associates with transformation principle demonstrated in Streptococcus pneumoniae.
- Oswald Avery, Colin MacLeod, Maclyn McCarty associate with biochemical proof that DNase inhibits transformation whereas proteases do not.
- Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase associate with unequivocal proof of DNA as genetic material using \(^{32}\text{P}\) and \(^{35}\text{S}\).
- Matthew Meselson and Franklin Stahl associate with semiconservative replication proof using \(^{15}\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}\) and CsCl gradient.

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
All methodology pairs align precisely with standard experimental accounts.
Final Answer: The correct matching is Frederick Griffith with Transformation principle demonstrated in Streptococcus pneumoniae; Oswald Avery, Colin MacLeod, Maclyn McCarty with Biochemical proof that DNase inhibits transformation whereas proteases do not; Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase with Unequivocal proof of DNA as genetic material using \(^{32}\text{P}\) and \(^{35}\text{S}\); and Matthew Meselson and Franklin Stahl with Semiconservative replication proof using \(^{15}\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}\) and CsCl gradient.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MOLECULAR_BASIS_OF_INHERITANCE_MCQ_Q04 - Match replication machinery components with specific roles

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Replication Component) List-II (Function / Characteristic)
A. DNA-dependent DNA polymerase I. Joins discontinuously synthesised fragments
B. Deoxyribonucleoside triphosphates II. Serves as origin where replication initiates
C. DNA ligase III. Polymerises deoxynucleotides exclusively in \(5'\rightarrow 3'\) direction
D. Origin of replication IV. Dual role as substrate and source of energy

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The question requires pairing enzymes and functional elements involved in prokaryotic DNA replication with their precise operational characteristics.

Step 2: Relevant Principles and Mechanisms
- DNA-dependent DNA polymerase is an efficient enzyme that catalyses polymerisation of deoxynucleotides with high fidelity strictly in the \(5'\rightarrow 3'\) direction on the newly synthesised strand.
- Deoxyribonucleoside triphosphates (dNTPs) serve dual purposes: acting as substrates for building the DNA polymer and providing high-energy phosphate bonds (through cleavage of the two terminal phosphates) to fuel the polymerisation reaction.
- DNA ligase catalyses the formation of phosphodiester bonds to covalently join discontinuously synthesised fragments (Okazaki fragments) on the lagging strand.
- Origin of replication is a definite sequence in the DNA where replication originates; without it, propagation and replication of DNA cannot occur.

Step 3: Pairing Identification
- DNA-dependent DNA polymerase associates with polymerising deoxynucleotides exclusively in \(5'\rightarrow 3'\) direction.
- Deoxyribonucleoside triphosphates associate with dual role as substrate and source of energy.
- DNA ligase associates with joining discontinuously synthesised fragments.
- Origin of replication associates with serving as origin where replication initiates.

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
All biochemical properties and physiological roles match the replication machinery described in the text.
Final Answer: The correct matching is DNA-dependent DNA polymerase with Polymerises deoxynucleotides exclusively in \(5'\rightarrow 3'\) direction; Deoxyribonucleoside triphosphates with Dual role as substrate and source of energy; DNA ligase with Joins discontinuously synthesised fragments; and Origin of replication with Serves as origin where replication initiates.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MOLECULAR_BASIS_OF_INHERITANCE_MCQ_Q05 - Match eukaryotic and bacterial RNA polymerases

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Polymerase / Catalytic RNA) List-II (Transcribed Product / Activity)
A. RNA polymerase I I. Heterogeneous nuclear RNA (hnRNA)
B. RNA polymerase II II. \(28\text{S}\), \(18\text{S}\), and \(5.8\text{S}\) rRNAs
C. RNA polymerase III III. Ribozyme forming peptide bonds during translation
D. Bacterial \(23\text{S}\) rRNA IV. tRNA, \(5\text{S}\) rRNA, and snRNAs

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The problem focuses on division of labour among eukaryotic nuclear RNA polymerases and the catalytic function of bacterial ribosomal RNA.

Step 2: Relevant Principles of Transcription and Translation
- In eukaryotic nuclei, RNA polymerase I is responsible for transcribing ribosomal RNAs, namely the \(28\text{S}\), \(18\text{S}\), and \(5.8\text{S}\) rRNAs.
- RNA polymerase II transcribes the precursor of messenger RNA, known as heterogeneous nuclear RNA (hnRNA).
- RNA polymerase III transcribes transfer RNA (tRNA), \(5\text{S}\) rRNA, and small nuclear RNAs (snRNAs).
- In bacteria, the \(23\text{S}\) rRNA functions as a catalytic RNA molecule (ribozyme) that catalyses the formation of peptide bonds during protein synthesis.

Step 3: Pairing Identification
- RNA polymerase I associates with \(28\text{S}\), \(18\text{S}\), and \(5.8\text{S}\) rRNAs.
- RNA polymerase II associates with heterogeneous nuclear RNA (hnRNA).
- RNA polymerase III associates with tRNA, \(5\text{S}\) rRNA, and snRNAs.
- Bacterial \(23\text{S}\) rRNA associates with ribozyme forming peptide bonds during translation.

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
The specificity of RNA synthesis and RNA-mediated catalysis confirms that each assigned pair is biochemically exact.
Final Answer: The correct matching is RNA polymerase I with \(28\text{S}\), \(18\text{S}\), and \(5.8\text{S}\) rRNAs; RNA polymerase II with Heterogeneous nuclear RNA (hnRNA); RNA polymerase III with tRNA, \(5\text{S}\) rRNA, and snRNAs; and Bacterial \(23\text{S}\) rRNA with Ribozyme forming peptide bonds during translation.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MOLECULAR_BASIS_OF_INHERITANCE_MCQ_Q06 - Match RNA processing and noncoding features

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Process / Structural Region) List-II (Biochemical Definition)
A. Splicing I. Addition of methyl guanosine triphosphate to the \(5'\)-end
B. Capping II. Removal of introns and joining of exons in a defined order
C. Tailing III. Sequences present at both ends of mRNA required for efficient translation
D. Untranslated regions (UTRs) IV. Addition of 200–300 adenylate residues at the \(3'\)-end

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The task requires matching post-transcriptional modifications of eukaryotic primary transcripts (hnRNA) and untranslated structural features of mRNA with their biochemical descriptions.

Step 2: Relevant Principles and Post-transcriptional Events
- Splicing is the molecular process by which non-coding intervening sequences (introns) are excised from primary transcripts and coding sequences (exons) are joined together in a defined sequence to produce mature mRNA.
- Capping involves the covalent attachment of an unusual modified nucleotide, 7-methylguanosine triphosphate (\(\text{m}^7\text{G}_{\text{ppp}}\)), to the \(5'\)-end of the nascent hnRNA.
- Tailing (polyadenylation) consists of the template-independent enzymatic addition of 200 to 300 adenylate residues at the \(3'\)-end of the RNA.
- Untranslated regions (UTRs) are nucleotide segments present on mature mRNA before the initiation codon at the \(5'\)-end and after the stop codon at the \(3'\)-end that are essential for efficient translation.

Step 3: Pairing Identification
- Splicing associates with removal of introns and joining of exons in a defined order.
- Capping associates with addition of methyl guanosine triphosphate to the \(5'\)-end.
- Tailing associates with addition of 200–300 adenylate residues at the \(3'\)-end.
- Untranslated regions (UTRs) associate with sequences present at both ends of mRNA required for efficient translation.

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
Each operational definition corresponds unequivocally to its post-transcriptional or mRNA structural counterpart.
Final Answer: The correct matching is Splicing with Removal of introns and joining of exons in a defined order; Capping with Addition of methyl guanosine triphosphate to the \(5'\)-end; Tailing with Addition of 200–300 adenylate residues at the \(3'\)-end; and Untranslated regions (UTRs) with Sequences present at both ends of mRNA required for efficient translation.

Final Answer: The correct matching is z gene with \(\beta\)-galactosidase; y gene with Permease; a gene with Transacetylase; and i gene with Repressor protein.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MOLECULAR_BASIS_OF_INHERITANCE_MCQ_Q08 - Match codons and genetic code properties

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Codon / Characteristic) List-II (Feature / Assigned Meaning)
A. AUG I. Polynucleotide phosphorylase used for template-independent RNA synthesis
B. UAA, UAG, UGA II. Codes specifically for Phenylalanine
C. UUU III. Dual functions: codes for Methionine and acts as initiator codon
D. Severo Ochoa enzyme IV. Stop or termination codons that do not code for any amino acid

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The problem requires matching specific triplet codons and enzymatic tools of genetic code elucidation with their biochemical attributes.

Step 2: Relevant Principles of the Genetic Code
- The triplet codon AUG possesses dual functions: it encodes the amino acid methionine and serves as the initiator codon for translation.
- The three codons UAA, UAG, and UGA do not code for any amino acids; they lack corresponding aminoacyl-tRNAs and therefore function as stop or termination codons.
- The homopolymer codon UUU was the first triplet deciphered and codes unambiguously for phenylalanine.
- Severo Ochoa enzyme is polynucleotide phosphorylase, which was instrumental in deciphering the code because it polymerises RNA with defined sequences in a template-independent manner.

Step 3: Pairing Identification
- AUG associates with dual functions: codes for Methionine and acts as initiator codon.
- UAA, UAG, UGA associate with stop or termination codons that do not code for any amino acid.
- UUU associates with coding specifically for Phenylalanine.
- Severo Ochoa enzyme associates with polynucleotide phosphorylase used for template-independent RNA synthesis.

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
Each codon assignment and biochemical definition corresponds precisely to the genetic code rules.
Final Answer: The correct matching is AUG with Dual functions: codes for Methionine and acts as initiator codon; UAA, UAG, UGA with Stop or termination codons that do not code for any amino acid; UUU with Codes specifically for Phenylalanine; and Severo Ochoa enzyme with Polynucleotide phosphorylase used for template-independent RNA synthesis.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_MOLECULAR_BASIS_OF_INHERITANCE_MCQ_Q10 - Match DNA fingerprinting methods and terms

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Method / Component) List-II (Role in DNA Profiling)
A. Alec Jeffreys I. Cleaves high molecular weight genomic DNA at specific sites
B. Restriction endonucleases II. Mini-satellite tandem repeats ranging from \(0.1\text{ to }20\text{ kb}\) used as probes
C. Agarose gel electrophoresis III. Developed the original DNA fingerprinting technique
D. Variable Number of Tandem Repeats (VNTR) IV. Separates cut DNA fragments according to size

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
The task requires matching techniques, scientists, and molecular markers integral to DNA fingerprinting with their functional definitions.

Step 2: Relevant Principles of DNA Fingerprinting
- Sir Alec Jeffreys developed the original technique of DNA fingerprinting using satellite DNA probes displaying high polymorphism.
- Restriction endonucleases are molecular scissors that digest and cleave long genomic DNA into manageable fragments at specific recognition sequences.
- Agarose gel electrophoresis is the analytical separation technique that resolves negatively charged DNA fragments on the basis of their molecular size.
- Variable Number of Tandem Repeats (VNTR) belongs to mini-satellite DNA repeats where short sequence units are tandemly repeated, varying in size from \(0.1\text{ to }20\text{ kb}\), serving as highly polymorphic radiolabelled probes during Southern blot hybridisation.

Step 3: Pairing Identification
- Alec Jeffreys associates with developing the original DNA fingerprinting technique.
- Restriction endonucleases associate with cleaving high molecular weight genomic DNA at specific sites.
- Agarose gel electrophoresis associates with separating cut DNA fragments according to size.
- Variable Number of Tandem Repeats (VNTR) associates with mini-satellite tandem repeats ranging from \(0.1\text{ to }20\text{ kb}\) used as probes.

Step 4: Check and Final Answer
Each technological step matches its operational mechanism in forensic and paternity DNA analysis.
Final Answer: The correct matching is Alec Jeffreys with Developed the original DNA fingerprinting technique; Restriction endonucleases with Cleaves high molecular weight genomic DNA at specific sites; Agarose gel electrophoresis with Separates cut DNA fragments according to size; and Variable Number of Tandem Repeats (VNTR) with Mini-satellite tandem repeats ranging from \(0.1\text{ to }20\text{ kb}\) used as probes.
